Body: This newly added value is mojibake: UTF-8 bytes were decoded as CP437, so the policy-blocked message renders unreadably in this locale. Re-decode the value as UTF-8 (equivalent to `value.encode("cp437").decode("utf-8")`) to recover the intended translation.

`inject_ready_cloud_catalog` first writes `cloud_models` into `_meta.wta`, but this second `inject_wta_meta` call replaces that entire namespace rather than merging it. Because the new identity metadata is now injected unconditionally, every initialize response with a ready host cloud catalog loses the catalog before reaching the helper, breaking the model picker for those agents. Build one trusted `WtaMeta` containing the catalog, resolved identity, and proposal capability, then inject it once.

This E2E only reads the persisted setting back; it never opens a session or observes the Terminal → helper → ACP default being applied. Nevertheless, its checklist mapping credits the stronger C286 contract that the setting “supplies the default for new sessions.” Add a deterministic assertion for the initial provider-native `on` operation before any `/yolo` command, or narrow the checklist item.

This does not enforce the documented exact Copilot contract requiring both `on` and `off`: when the current value is another advertised value, `{on, current}` is accepted even if `off` is absent. Since this enables a high-risk provider mode, require the configured restore value as part of capability validation.

These live Copilot tests treat an installed but unauthenticated CLI as ready, then fail at `Wait-AgentReady` even though authentication is an external prerequisite. Determine readiness with `Get-AgentCliStatus` (retaining a separate installed-only flag if desired for the settings round-trip case) so unauthenticated environments are reported as skips rather than product failures.

The selector search stops at the first matching id/category before checking that it is a `Select`. A malformed non-Select entry can therefore hide a later valid selector, causing supported Yolo mode to be rejected. Continue searching until the id, category, and kind all match, as `model_option_from_config` does.

The search stops at the first matching id/category before checking its kind. If an agent advertises a same-named non-Select entry before the valid Select entry, capability discovery incorrectly fails instead of continuing to the valid selector. Include the kind check in the predicate, as the model-selector path does.

The PR description promises `session/request_permission` fallback auto-approval (`AllowOnce`) for non-native/unsupported contracts, but this implementation explicitly keeps every ordinary permission request interactive and instead adds native modes for Claude, Codex, and Gemini. That materially changes the advertised behavior and title; either restore the documented fallback or update the PR description to the provider-native-only contract.

The override is removed for `/new`, but the other session teardown paths `drop_tab_session` and `reset_tab_session_for` remove their `session_to_tab` entries without removing the corresponding Yolo override or pending change. That leaks per-session state and can auto-approve a later session if an ACP server reuses the ID—the same reuse case this cleanup is intended to prevent. Apply the same `remove_session`/pending cleanup in every teardown path.

The matrix promises to skip unavailable providers, but it checks only whether the executable exists. An installed, unauthenticated Claude/Codex/Gemini proceeds and fails readiness instead of being recorded as an external-prerequisite skip, unlike the established AgentMatrix suite. Gate each case on `Get-AgentCliStatus -eq 'authed'`.

The mapped C292 contract says policy overrides a stored global-on default and rejects `/yolo on`, but this test asserts only the slash-command rejection. It would still pass if startup incorrectly enabled provider-native Yolo despite the policy. Assert the initial session is reconciled off (or that no native-on operation occurs) before checking the command.

The lazy-session operation can apply a stale enable after a settings/GPO update. If `agent_config_changed` was queued before `SessionAttached` but is handled while this awaited RPC is in flight, the App sees no bound session and schedules no replacement operation; this task then completes the old enable and proceeds to the prompt even though the shared effective state is now off. Re-read the effective state after the RPC and synchronously apply any changed desired value (failing closed on disable failure) before allowing the first prompt.

The implementation now defines provider-native contracts for Claude (and below, Codex/Gemini), while ordinary permission requests remain interactive. This contradicts the PR description's “Copilot-native only; all other agents use AllowOnce fallback” approval paths. The code and design spec agree with each other, so update the PR description to describe the implemented security model before merge.

The `/config` path has the same acknowledgement gap: it returns `Some(config_options)` after any successful RPC even if the provider reports that the native Yolo option did not change to `value`. The App then clears `native_yolo_config_pending` and reports success, and a failed native disable can escape the fail-closed restart path. Require the returned native option to report the requested current value before returning success.  This issue also appears on line 450 of the same file.

The `{Locked}` annotation includes `/yolo`, but `/yolo` does not occur in this resource value. Locked-token comments are consumed as translator constraints and must name tokens actually present; remove `/yolo` from the annotation (the command name is rendered separately).

Passing the broad `Software\Policies\Microsoft` key means this recursive watcher fires for policy changes belonging to every Microsoft product, causing unnecessary full settings reloads. Pass `PolicyRegKey` instead; `CreatePolicyChangeWatcher` already falls back to the deepest existing ancestor when the product key does not exist.

Nothing constructs `ChatMessage::Status`; repository-wide references are limited to this variant and its new renderer/theme constant. This leaves an unreachable rendering path in the state model. Remove the variant, renderer arm, and style constant, or add the intended producer and focused coverage.

For Copilot, this accepts `allow_all` without the required `off` value whenever its current value is some other advertised value: the checks only require `on` plus the current value, which is then captured as the restore value. That weakens the exact selector contract described by this PR and can treat a lookalike option as the privileged allow-all control. Require Copilot's complete `on`/`off` value set before enabling native Yolo.

Capability discovery stops at the first matching id/category before checking its kind. A non-`Select` entry can therefore hide a later valid selector, incorrectly disabling native Yolo for an otherwise supported provider. Include the kind check in the search so discovery continues past incompatible entries.

Canonical Copilot sessions without the verified selector are supposed to use the `request_permission` fallback, but this condition makes fallback one-way: `/yolo on` succeeds through interception, while a later `/yolo off` always errors and leaves the local override enabled because `copilot_requires_native_disable()` is true even when native mode was never applied. Track native-selector/native-enable state per session so a missing selector only blocks disabling when that session may actually have native `allow_all=on`; otherwise acknowledge the fallback opt-out.

A settings/GPO disable can race this startup enable. `effective()` is checked before the awaited RPC, while `SessionAttached` is emitted only afterward. If the runtime update arrives during that await, `apply_runtime_yolo_config` sees no live session and queues an empty reconciliation; this RPC can then leave Copilot native `allow_all` enabled even though the shared state (or policy) is off. Re-check the effective state after the enable completes and synchronously undo it (triggering fail-closed restart on failure), or serialize session creation with runtime reconciliation.
